title: Student sleep health and school start times
asked: Dr Choo Pei Ling asked whether the Government tracks insufficient sleep among school-going children and adolescents, and what measures are being considered to improve sleep health.
response: MOE monitors sleep sufficiency by surveying Primary 5 and Secondary 3 students; the 2025 survey found they got seven hours of sleep on average on school days, a slight increase from 2023. Schools teach healthy sleep habits, self-management and time management through PE and Character and Citizenship Education, and from January this year secondary students' personal learning devices default to sleep mode at 10.30 pm. MOE also works with KK Women's and Children's Hospital to engage parents on sleep health and gives screen-use tips via social media, and will continue through Grow Well SG.

key_points.point: MOE monitors sleep sufficiency by surveying Primary 5 and Secondary 3 students.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: The Ministry of Education (MOE) monitors sleep sufficiency by surveying Primary 5 and Secondary 3 students.

key_points.point: The 2025 survey found Primary 5 and Secondary 3 students got seven hours of sleep on average on school days, a slight increase from 2023.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Primary 5 and Secondary 3 students reported getting seven hours of sleep on average on school days, with a slight increase compared to 2023.

key_points.point: Schools teach healthy sleep habits, self-management and time management through Physical Education and Character and Citizenship Education lessons.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: students are taught healthy sleep habits, self-management and time management skills through Physical Education, and Character and Citizenship Education lessons.

key_points.point: From January this year, secondary school students' personal learning devices default to sleep mode at 10.30 pm.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Starting from January this year, the personal learning devices for secondary school students have been set by default to go into sleep mode earlier at 10.30 pm.

key_points.point: MOE partners with KK Women's and Children's Hospital to engage parents on practical ways to support students' sleep health.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: MOE, in partnership with KK Women's and Children's Hospital, has engaged parents on practical ways to support students' sleep health through engagement sessions with medical experts on sleep matters.

key_points.point: MOE will continue working with other Ministries and agencies through Grow Well SG to help children inculcate healthy sleep habits.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: MOE will continue to work with other Ministries and agencies through Grow Well SG to help our children inculcate healthy sleep habits.

key_points.point: There is no data on students' sleep quality at this point.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: We do not have data with regard to their sleep quality at this point of time.

key_points.point: Schools have autonomy to decide start times, which are no earlier than 7.30 am.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: schools are given the autonomy to decide on their start time. They start no earlier than 7.30 am.

key_points.point: Pushing back school start times could mean lessons continue into the hot afternoon, which may be less ideal for learning.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: when we push back school start time, it would also mean that lessons might continue well into the afternoon when it can also be hot and humid, and perhaps less ideal for learning.

left_open: Whether the Ministry has considered assessing sleep quality.
Whether later school start times will be piloted for older students.
supplementary: Supplementary questions asked about assessing sleep quality and piloting later school start times.
